content.en: I am 32 years old. I was born in a small village in Rampur zilla of Uttar Pradesh. We were eleven brothers and sisters, that is what my mother said. Only three of us survived. One brother, one sister and I. When I was seventeen my elder sister drowned herself in a well. Her mother-in-law used to beat her and abuse her constantly. She was given more work than she could possibly do. In desperation she killed herself, leaving behind one daughter and one son.

When was I married? I don't remember. Possibly when I was twelve or thirteen years old. After six years I went to live with my husband. He was a Kisan. He leased land and we earned enough to live on. My mother had given me a buffalo which I took care of. I milked it, fed it, cleaned it and sold ghee and butter. I also kept some chicken. At the end of the week I always had some money. My husband always took this away.

Morning, noon, and night I worked. My mother died, so I also took care of my brother's house. I looked after 4 of our animals and six of his, cutting grass, cleaning both the houses and cooking. I cannot give you an account of the work I have done in my life. It is too much.

My husband was always quarreling with me. He did not love me or the children. When my son was sick, I had to take him to the doctor. Once, I was also unwell. The child and I were both vomiting, but he did not accompany us. Somehow, I managed to save my son, though he had money he refused to give it, I had to walk miles to get to the doctor. He only loved his money. He harassed me constantly, threatening to sell my buffalo every week at the local market. I somehow begged and persuaded him not to. Twice he also beat me and I resolved that I could not live with such indignity.
Though I loved my brother very much and did all his work in the house, he also did not care for me. For very small things, he would also beat me and I felt I could not go to his house for help.
For many weeks I cried every day and wondered whether I should kill myself. Then I worried about what would happen to my children. I decided to go away with my children after Ramzan.

Now it is six years since I left home and three years since I came to Delhi. A family I knew for twenty years helped me to get a job in Allahabad. But they also cheated me. I kept 3 tolas of gold and nine hundred rupees in their custody. After one year when I asked for it, they avoided talking about it and then said they cannot give it back because they had used it up for their son's marriage. What could I do? In Allahabad I worked in a house for Rs. twenty a month. I used to work from 4 a.m. in the morning till midnight everyday with- out holidays and could not save any money. My daughter meanwhile was working with a family in Delhi and I decided to also come and work in Delhi.

Finding work was not easy. I walked for miles in Nizamuddin looking for work. People turned me out saying "there is no work here". An old couple gave me shelter in their Jhuggi and as soon as I got work, I rented a house. I was forced to change maliks many times because they would give too much work and too little money. One malik accused me of theft when I went to ask for my wages and locked me in his house. I somehow escaped and went to lodge a police complaint. I came to know that this man behaved badly with all his servants.

One day the jamadarni told me I should go to the Saheli office and they would help me to find work, I did not find more work, but I have become a part of Saheli. I have been helped and I also give help to other women. We meet in the basti once a week and discuss our problems, about work, husbands, children and many other things. For the last few months my room has also been used as a shelter. Women from the age of sixteen to forty-five along with them. Children have shared my house. I feel we women have to help each other.
“Sakina people say women can't live alone, they need a man, protection, don’t you have problems?"

I feel a single woman can live comfortably if she is willing to work hard. I live with both my child- ren and am educating them. I have always worked in the village, in my mother's house, in my husband's house and now. People respect me because I work and earn my living and do not do any wrong things. Sometimes men have tried to make suggestions, but I clearly tell them that I believe in work and do not want any favours. I ask all women, what is the use of going from one man to another? Is our life only in the hands of men? Can't we think, don't we work hard? I feel people will respect us if we learn to be independent and respect ourselves.
